problem.title: Couchbase VBucket Rebalance Failures During Autoscaling Events
problem.prompt: Couchbase cluster automatically scaling out from 10 to 15 nodes under peak load.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Never execute storage cluster rebalancing or partition migrations during peak production traffic hours."
Production Hardening: Revocations Trigger rebalances strictly during off-peak traffic windows, throttle rebalance concurrency bandwidth, and pre-warm nodes before joining the active cluster .
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.

stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: I/O Latency → max.poll Exceeded → Eager Revoke → 💥 Lag.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Balloons to Millions Initiating a node rebalance while the cluster is running at 90% CPU and network saturation. Rebalance traffic competes with production traffic, causing node heartbeats to fail, aborting the rebalance midway and leaving vBuckets orphaned.
Breakdown Chain: I/O Latency → max.poll Exceeded → Eager Revoke → 💥 Lag
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.

approachSteps: 1. Track real-time latency gradients and inflight concurrency.
2. Reject excess traffic at the ingress boundary within <0.1ms.
3. Monitor P99 latency and verify autonomous recovery when downstream pressure subsides.
